assessment: This paper challenges the widely held view that the number of naive T cells in our body is regulated through homeostatic feedback mechanisms, meaning that cells divide more frequently – or live longer – when cell numbers are low. The arguments in favor of this homeostatic regulation rely on cross-sectional data, which fail to distinguish between the effects of host age, cell age, and cell numbers, each of which separately may influence the dynamics of cells. Using a set of mathematical models and experimental data sets, this paper manages to tear these factors apart and reports that in mice there is no feedback regulation of naive T cell numbers.
